scenes.title: Three Questions
scenes.summary: For accusation and defense we must grasp why people do wrong, in what state they are, and whom they wrong.

scenes.title: Doing Wrong
scenes.summary: Doing wrong is causing harm voluntarily against the law, particular or common; voluntary acts are done knowingly and without compulsion, and what is chosen is known. People choose to harm from vice and lack of self-control, each in his own field: the mean man over money, the coward in danger, the shameless from contempt for reputation.

scenes.title: Seven Causes
scenes.summary: All actions come either not through the agent, by chance, nature or force, or through him, by habit or longing; longing is rational, which is wish for the good, or irrational, anger and appetite. So there are seven causes: chance, nature, force, habit, reasoning, temper and appetite.

scenes.title: Not Age or Wealth
scenes.summary: Age, wealth and poverty are not causes: the young act from anger and appetite, the poor from need and the rich from plenty, but the causes are the same. What matters is what usually follows from such circumstances, which will be discussed later.

scenes.title: The Seven Defined
scenes.summary: Chance has an indefinite cause and no purpose; nature an ordered cause within; force acts against appetite and reasoning; habit comes from repetition; reasoning chooses the advantageous; temper and anger seek revenge, which differs from punishment; appetite seeks the pleasant. All voluntary acts aim at what is or seems good or pleasant, so the pleasant must be defined.
